_comment: Engine calls whose 42.20.2 Java bodies were READ and found unable to throw on a
non-nil receiver - trivial field returns, or fully null-checked. Wrapping one of
these in pcall is dead weight, and check-pcall.py fails the build for it.
ADDING TO THIS LIST IS A DECOMPILE JOB. Open the class in
PZ_Engine_Decompiled_42.20.2-ffe7a8a4b1/, read the method body, and put the
class:line you read under 'verified'. A grep hit on the symbol is not a reading
of the method - that assumption is how the suite reached 1,299 guards.
NOT eligible, no matter how harmless the name looks: anything that dereferences
a static singleton (getCell before a world exists), anything that throws by
design (SandboxOptions.set), vanilla LUA functions (not in the decompile at all,
so unverifiable here), and any callback owned by another mod.
THE CHECK MATCHES ON METHOD NAME, NOT TYPE - Lua gives it no receiver type. So a
name earns its place only if it is trivial on EVERY class that could plausibly
receive it in this codebase. getName is the counterexample that set this rule:
trivial on Item (a field return) but NOT on CharacterTrait, where it resolves
stale registry object - precisely the failure MMSnapshotCodec guards on purpose.
One shared name would have had the checker demand the deletion of a load-bearing
guard. When a name is trivial on one class and risky on another, leave it off.

a closed connection, so 'the player may have disconnected' needs no guard.

IsoObject.setOutlineHighlight:5133/5154 and setOutlineHighlightCol:5083-5118
are safe (lazy FBORenderObjectOutline singleton, per-player array writes)
but they touch a render singleton rather than returning a field, so they

2026-08-13, RFTDLimes pass:
IsoObject.getSquare:1126 - `return this.square`. The name was already
enforced via IsoMovingObject:534 (current-else-square, both fields), so
this closes the other class that receives it in this codebase.
IsoGridSquare.getX:6331 / getY:6335 / getZ:6339 - field returns. The names
were already enforced via IsoMovingObject; recorded here because Limes
reads coordinates off a SQUARE, not off a moving object.
IsoFireManager.Remove:166 - FireStack.contains then FireStack.remove, with
an early return and a println for an unknown fire. FireStack is a static
final ArrayList (:64). This is the second class to receive the name
`Remove` (ItemContainer.Remove:1940 was the first) and it is trivial on
both, so the name keeps its place under the shared-name rule.
NOT added, deliberately, from this pass:
IsoCell.getZombieList:2339 IS a field return (`return this.zombieList`)
and IsoCell is the only class in 42.20.2 declaring the name - but it is
almost always written as getCell():getZombieList(), and getCell() is the
hazard the guard is really for (it dereferences IsoWorld.instance,
unguarded, before a world exists). Listing the name made the checker
demand the deletion of RQReflect.lua:110, a load-bearing guard. Left off
for exactly the getName reason. The fix at a call site is to step
through IsoWorld.instance and drop the guard, which is what LMZeds and
LMZedsCl now do - not to trust the name.
getSpecificPlayer (LuaManager:3617) is `IsoPlayer.players[player]` - safe
for the literal 0 that Limes passes, but a computed index out of that
four-slot array throws, so the NAME is not safe and stays off.
TextManager.getFontHeight:127 calls getFontFromEnum and dereferences the
result with no null check - a font this build lacks is an NPE. Guards on
it are load-bearing wherever a measured line height has a fallback.
Clipboard.getClipboard:36 cannot throw (catch(Throwable) around the GLFW
read, cached value off the main thread) but it is a static on a class
that may be absent, so callers want `Clipboard and ...`, not a bare call.
setLx / setLy DO NOT EXIST anywhere in 42.20.2 (setX:478 and setY:495 do).
Any Lua calling them throws, so those guards are load-bearing - see
LMRestrictCl.bounce.
2026-08-13, RFTDHusbandry pass:
REMOVED getFullName (was listed under a 'ScriptItem' key that does not
exist in 42.20.2 - the class is zombie/scripting/objects/Item, whose
getFullName:907 IS `return this.moduleDotType`). The NAME fails the
shared-name rule outright: VehicleScript.getFullName:1674 is

(RCNoVanilla:349/566/728/885, which say so in their own comments, and

Item's is a field, but one shared name cannot cover the other two.

IsoAnimal:259-275 returns early from the constructor on
checkForChickenpocalypse/checkForWater/adef==null, so callers nil-check
the result. That early return is why isBaby:1657 (getData().currentStage),
getAge:2101, isGeriatric:1809 (this.adef), setAgeDebug:1500,
getMaxAgeGeriatric (AnimalData:1533) and setSize/setWeight
(AnimalData:1380/1598, clamped through getMinSize/getMaxSize ->
parent.adef) all stay guarded in HBLifespan - none of them is listed.
IsoAnimal.getAnimalType:1487 - `return this.type`. AnimalDefinitions:699
is the other receiver of the name and is `return this.animalTypeStr`.
IsoAnimal.isWild:2926 - `return this.wild`.
AnimalData.getSize:1389 / getWeight:1409 - field returns. getWeight's other
receiver in this codebase is Nutrition:296, also a field return. setWeight
is NOT listed: Nutrition.setWeight:300 damages the player and fires
OnPlayerGetDamage below 35kg.
IsoHutch.isSlave:827, isOpen:616, isAllDoorClosed:985,
isEggHatchDoorOpen:942 - field reads. getDeadBody:906, getNestBox:961,

IsoCell.getObjectListForLua:2315 - snapshots objectList, a `private final`
HashSet initialised at IsoCell:165.
IsoGridSquare.getObjects:8005 - `return this.objects`.
IsoMovingObject.getCurrentSquare:1819 - `return this.current`.
NOT added, deliberately, from this pass:
IsoHutch.getAnimalInside:898 (`return this.animalInside`) and
getAnimal:902 (`animalInside.get(index)`) ARE trivial, and IsoHutch is
the only class receiving either name here - but HBKeepAlive.refillHutch
and HBLifespan.visitHutchAnimals wrap them in a DELIBERATE one-shot
cross-build probe (the B42 hutch API is young; a rename in a later 42.x

Same reason IsoZombie.getOwnerPlayer is off the list.
IsoHutch.getMaxAnimals:910 / getMaxNestBox:917 / getEnterSpotX:924 /
getEnterSpotY:931 / haveEggHatchDoor:938 all read this.def.rawgetInt or
rawgetStr with no null guard, and def is null for any hutch the

documents. getEntrySq:950 and getAllHutchObjects:858 chain through
getSquare().getCell() as well. All stay guarded.
IsoAnimal.updateLastTimeSinceUpdate:1561 goes through the
GameTime.getInstance() singleton; Stats.set:80 clamps via the
CharacterStat argument and NPEs on a null one. Neither is listed, so
the refill guards in HBKeepAlive/HBCommands keep their place.
setX / setY / setZ (IsoMovingObject:478/495/512) ARE field sets and the
teleport call sites now use them directly, but the names are also
ISUIElement's throughout the UI code, so they stay off the list.
isFemale is not listed: IsoGameCharacter:9312 resolves through
getCharacterGender() -> this.descriptor and AnimalData:1413 through
parent.getDescriptor(), and an animal from a bailed constructor has

getAnimals is not listed: BaseVehicle:9528 is a field return but
IsoGridSquare:9137 rebuilds the list by walking getMovingObjects().

allocates from a thread-local predicate pool - overload dispatch through

dereferences this.def after initSpriteInstance().
